correctness.rationale: The derivation is a direct finite-word proof: the substitution creates no cyclic 11; even and odd rotations form four strictly ordered prefix classes 0001,0010,01,1; within each class the source-rotation order reverses; preceding letters yield the exact BWT recursion; simple boundary induction yields 2m-2 runs for m>=2. The m=1 base is explicit. Standard-library independent cyclic rank-doubling checks agree for m=1..13, and naive full-rotation sorting agrees for m=1..9. Numerical checks are not substitutes for the all-m proof. The statement excludes suffix BWT and non-dyadic lengths.

originality.rationale: Direct searches for exact cyclic BWT, run-length sequence, reversed-complement recurrence, period-doubling substitution, and related morphic-word theorems revealed no covering exact transform or run-count result. Full-text comparison with the 2019 Thue–Morse transform theorem (different morphism), 2022 logarithmic bounds (not exact), 2023 morphism sensitivity result (different quantifiers), and 2025 follow-up (sensitivity, not iterates) leaves the exact fixed-point recursion and 2m-2 formula unproved by those sources. The closest indexed period-doubling records concern attractors and dynamical lifts, not the cyclic BWT. Originality is assessed relative to the available corpus; undiscovered equivalents remain a risk.

value.rationale: Run-length BWT is a standard compression and indexing measure. This gives the complete transform and exact run count of a canonical aperiodic primitive-morphism family, not a routine specialization of the known O(log n) bound. The proof reveals a four-class interleaving mechanism absent from generic order-reversal observations, and the finite recurrence yields all run lengths without lexicographically sorting 2^m rotations. The exact coefficient and word output are natural algorithmic refinements with independent mathematical interest; the scope is limited to the cyclic transform of dyadic period-doubling words.
